title: Sugar Research and Development Services Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a funding and accountability framework for an industry-owned company delivering research and development services for Australia's sugar industry.
The Minister could contract with a company, declare it the industry services body and fund its eligible work using levies and Commonwealth matching payments.
It would begin the day after Royal Assent, while companion legislation would handle changes to the levy and the existing research corporation's transition.
changes: Annual matching payments would be limited to the lesser of half eligible research spending or 0.5 per cent of sugar cane production value.
Unmatched eligible research expenditure could be carried forward into later years.
The industry body would have to comply with ministerial directions responding to exceptional, urgent circumstances in the national interest.
New or varied funding contracts would require tabling in both Houses within 15 sitting days.
summary.affected: The industry services company, sugar cane growers and millers, and the Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the companion Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, which transfers 75 per cent of the Sugar Research and Development Corporation's assets to the new industry body on its declaration and winds up the corporation by 30 September 2013, with the levy increase taking effect from 1 July 2013.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills as a reform backed by most of the industry, under which Sugar Research Australia would replace separate research bodies and receive a 70c per tonne levy paid equally by growers and mills, while raising concerns about consultation, regional research, conflicts of interest and the legislation's rushed 1 July 2013 commencement.

speeches.speaker: Paul Neville
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills and the creation of Sugar Research Australia, funded by a 70c per tonne levy, while urging the government and new board to retain research talent and address concerns about consultation, miller contributions, diversification and the closure of the Bundaberg research facility.

speeches.speaker: George Christensen
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills, saying they would consolidate research functions in Sugar Research Australia, reduce duplication and secure funding through a 70c per tonne levy, while urging swift passage to provide certainty for research staff and the industry's future.
